title: Bank account and entity volume drive integration and testing effort
decision_implication: Treat rollout as multi-wave with bank onboarding factory, not a simple configuration project.
rfp_implication: Add bank connectivity matrix, bank test plan, and named bank onboarding lead requirements.
cost_implication: Increase SIT, UAT, cutover, and hypercare effort assumptions.
risk_implication: Surface bank onboarding delay and reconciliation failure risk.
applies: Multi-entity treasury rollout with more than four banks or twelve accounts.
anti_pattern: Do not accept fixed-price implementation without validated account and bank scope.

title: ERP heterogeneity raises reconciliation and return-file complexity
decision_implication: Require ERP feed proof before vendor shortlisting.
rfp_implication: Ask vendors to provide ERP-specific feed mapping, ACK/NACK handling, and GL reconciliation approach.
scoring_implication: Increase ERP integration and data quality weights.
cost_implication: Increase integration lead and data engineering effort.
risk_implication: Surface T+1 cash reconciliation and data-quality risk.
applies: Multiple ERPs, custom extracts, or mixed SaaS/on-prem estate.
does_not_apply: Single modern ERP with standard Kyriba connector already implemented.
anti_pattern: Do not let vendors answer generically about ERP experience without feed-level evidence.

title: Portal-only controls are a fraud and audit-risk signal
evidence_trigger: approval_model contains portal-only OR first-time payee callback is manual
decision_implication: Make controls and entitlement governance first-class scope.
rfp_implication: Require dual-control workflows, callback audit trail, and entitlement review evidence.
cost_implication: Add controls design, IAM, and audit-readiness workstream effort.
risk_implication: Surface BEC, SoD, and audit deficiency risks.
applies: Treasury currently relies on bank portals, email approvals, or spreadsheets.
does_not_apply: Kyriba-equivalent controls already live and audited.
anti_pattern: Do not treat bank connectivity as a technical-only task.

title: Run-cost savings require a support model, not just automation
decision_implication: Business case must separate build cost, run cost, and retained-client effort.
rfp_implication: Ask vendors for steady-state support model, named runbook ownership, and hypercare exit criteria.
scoring_implication: Increase managed-service transition and knowledge-transfer weight.
cost_implication: Model year-one hypercare separately from steady-state run.
risk_implication: Surface benefit leakage if adoption and support transfer are weak.
applies: Significant manual work or external SI run support today.
does_not_apply: Already automated operation with internal support ownership.
anti_pattern: Do not claim run savings without support ownership and adoption proof.
